sections.name: mission
sections.value: You build ONE unit of plan 005-convo-ingest: the claude-native reader — Claude Code session jsonl plus subagent sidecars plus spilled tool-results, turned into RawRecords with byte-offset cursors. It must be independently written and tested behind the frozen ConversationSource trait, so the PM can compose it without reading your internals. You report to the PM, not to prime.

value.text: Orient: read your unit's row in docs/plans/005-convo-ingest/impl-guide.dd.md (BINDING, and read the AMENDED/RULING paragraphs in its architecture section — they correct the recipe with measurements), then crates/core/src/conversation_source.rs (the FROZEN contract) and crates/testkit/src/{conversation_source.rs,expectations.rs}. Run `harness instructions` and `harness boot --json` in YOUR worktree before changing anything. DOGFOOD FLOWSPACE: `flowspace3 search "<question>"` for every meaning-shaped question before grep (exact identifiers may still grep); report every miss or confusing envelope as friction.

Ack FIRST, before any code: `pij send pij-traditional-piranha` with your read of the unit and a NUMBERED implementation plan. I rule it by number. Corrections to this packet are welcome and expected — bring evidence, your measurement outranks my prose.

EXPORT YOUR SEAT ID BEFORE YOU MESSAGE ME: `export PIJ_SESSION_ID=<your pij id>` in the shell you send from. From a worktree, pij cannot infer your seat and your reply is silently lost otherwise. Verify with `pij whoami` before your ack.

THE CONTRACT IS FROZEN (2026-08-28). Fill it, never widen it. A method ConversationSource does not have, a type field you wish existed, a signature you would rather have — all of those are a STOP-AND-ASK to me, not a local edit. Three other coders compiled against the same shape; changing it is not a refactor, it is a re-plan.

NEVER `docker compose up`. Postgres is ALREADY running for the whole fleet as container flowspace3-db on host port 5433 (container_name is pinned in docker-compose.yml, so a second `up` collides and can take the fleet's database down). Your tests use the scratch database named in your scope, via FS3_TEST_DATABASE_URL — the harness testdb gate refuses a run that has not been told where it may write.

THE FIXTURES ARE BYTE-PINNED AND READ-ONLY TO YOU. crates/testkit/fixtures/conversations/** is committed and its sha256 is asserted on every test run by fs3_testkit::Expectations::verify_fixtures_unchanged. The contract suite writes on purpose (append and torn-line cases), so implement SourceFixture over a SCRATCH COPY in a tempdir — never over the committed bytes. If a fixture is genuinely wrong, that is a stop-and-ask to me: it is regenerated by a driver, not hand-edited.

Implement per the /builder implement discipline: tests alongside code, your unit's suite proving the contract with NO other unit present. Commit as you go with `harness commit` (conventional commits are BINDING — release-please reads them). Status card at the start and end of each work unit (`pij report now`).
Stay inside your fence (scope below). If the work forces you outside it, STOP and ask me — that is a composition concern and solving it unilaterally is how parallel units collide.

Done = `harness checks` green in YOUR OWN worktree + your unit's tests proving the contract + the snap-in recipe written. Report done to me with the evidence, then HOLD for composition questions. You never merge, never open a PR, never touch main.

Capture friction the moment it bites: `harness observe "<what>" --kind difficulty|confusion --workaround "<what you did>" --suggested-encoding "<how to fix it for the next agent>". LIST, never CLEAR — the buffer is shared across the fleet and clearing destroys your siblings' observations. Report anything surprising to me while you are still in context, not at the end.

YOUR STORE HAS NO ORACLE, and that is stated rather than hidden. The pinned reconvo.py has no claude-native reader at all, so crates/testkit/fixtures/conversations/claude/expectations.json makes a STRUCTURAL claim only, labelled PM-derived-not-oracle. Your mechanical done-bar is assert_ordinals_are_a_subsequence plus the contract suite; your semantic check arrives later, at the tk-c305 first-light transcript. Do not go looking for a claude oracle — the PM checked, and the metrics-db mirror of the same session covers a disjoint time window.

RECIPE GOTCHA 1 — PER-BLOCK MERGE, and the fixture is built to catch you: claude writes ONE LINE PER CONTENT BLOCK, so several `assistant` records share one message.id and must merge into ONE turn. The expectation file quantifies exactly how much merging is owed: session a5a5588f has 38 assistant records over 13 distinct message ids. A reader that emits 38 turns there is wrong.

RECIPE GOTCHA 6 — SIDECARS ARE CHILD CONVERSATIONS, NOT PARENT RECORDS. A subagent sidecar is its own conversation (SessionKind::Subagent, parent_session_id set); folding it into the parent's sequence makes both unreadable. And resolve() is called on EVERY poll precisely because a sidecar can appear mid-session — a reader that resolves once loses every subagent spawned after ingestion began. The fixture carries subagents/agent-aa8ccc51dce0404a8.jsonl and its .meta.json.

RECIPE GOTCHA 9 — SPILLED TOOL RESULTS: an oversized tool result is written to a separate FILE and the record only references it. The fixture carries tool-results/b8e9hq4my.txt under session b1d6f4fb. Resolve or follow it per the recipe; do not silently emit a turn whose body is a filename.

RECORD-TYPE ALLOWLIST: the fixture holds 13 distinct record types (assistant, user, attachment, last-prompt, custom-title, agent-name, mode, permission-mode, atis-latch, pr-link, file-history-delta, file-history-snapshot, queue-operation). Most are not turns. Decide the allowlist deliberately and write it down in your service page — the structural claim permits you to emit FEWER records than the store holds, never one it never wrote.

LINE FRAMING IS ALREADY BUILT AND TESTED — use crates/providers/src/conversation_sources/tail.rs (`read_lines`), do not write your own tail buffer. It owns the incremental read, rotation and truncation detection and the torn-line rule. Spend this unit on the claude DIALECT. If tail.rs is missing something you need, that is a stop-and-ask to the PM, not a private copy.
pij-traditional-piranha (the PM) is your ONLY upward interface: acks, questions, done reports. You never message prime (pij-instant-lynx) or Jordan directly unless my seat is dead.
DEFER to me: anything touching the frozen contract or its types, dependency additions, migration numbers, schema changes, another unit's paths, and anything in .harness/government/**.
YOURS to decide: your module's internal structure, your test names and helpers, the order you work the tasks, how you factor private helpers — as long as the contract and the fence hold.
Stop-and-ask with EVIDENCE beats guessing, and beats coding around a brief you believe is wrong. One question per message: one sentence of context, one sentence of ask.

value.fence: crates/providers/src/conversation_sources/claude.rs (new) + exactly ONE `pub mod claude;` line in that directory's mod.rs, kept alphabetical · crates/providers/tests/** for your unit tests · docs/services/convo-source-claude.md (new). NOTHING ELSE. The fixtures are read-only to you; core, testkit, store and the daemon are other people's fences. Your scratch database is fs3_convo_u1a: export FS3_TEST_DATABASE_URL=postgres://flowspace3:flowspace3@127.0.0.1:5433/fs3_convo_u1a (already created for you).
value.forbidden_note: Never touch another unit's paths, the committed fixtures, .harness/government/**, the plan's flow state, or another seat's worktree. Never `docker compose up`. Never merge, never open a PR, never push to main — the PM composes.

value.text: The unit implements the FROZEN ConversationSource contract as written — resolve() finds every file on EVERY call (sidecars appear mid-session), read_incremental() returns store-ordered COMPLETE records only, always a resumable cursor, and rescanned=true when the file rotated or truncated.

fs3_testkit::conversation_source_contract passes over your store's fixtures, through a SourceFixture implemented on a scratch copy. This is the mechanical definition of done for a reader — not review, not your own judgement.

The committed expectations pass: fs3_testkit::Expectations::assert_ordinals_are_a_subsequence for your store's sessions (your emitted RawRecord::ordinal values must be an in-order, repeat-free subsequence of the ids the store holds) plus, where your store has an oracle, assert_oracle_prose_appears. READ crates/testkit/fixtures/conversations/<store>/expectations.json's grade_of_proof field before you trust or blame it.
harness checks GREEN in your own worktree (fmt, clippy -D warnings, cargo test --all), with FS3_TEST_DATABASE_URL set to your scratch database.

THE SNAP-IN RECIPE is shipped with the unit (tenet 4): the exact wiring I will paste at the composition root — construction call, the one `pub mod` line, config shape, any registration — as a section in your unit's docs/services page. You write the recipe; you never wire it in yourself.

Done report to me: what shipped, the evidence (test names, counts), every deviation from this packet and why, and anything the composer must know. Include your observed rustc/cargo versions (tenet 10).
